Webear Aura

Hear who you choose.

An open-ear band for people with hearing loss in one ear. It brings sound across from your deaf side, lets you pick one voice, and taps the side a sound came from.

Why Aura exists

Only one ear hears

With hearing loss in one ear, sound reaches you from one side only.

No sense of direction

Sound localization is lost. A voice, a horn or a bike could be coming from anywhere.

The other side is silent

Anything said or happening on your deaf side goes unheard.

Loud rooms are hard

In a noisy place you can't pick one voice out from the rest.

Scroll to turn it
01 · FIT

Sits behind your head.

A thin band rests at the back. Two small pads touch the bone in front of each ear. Nothing goes in your ear canal.

02 · OPEN EARS

You still hear the street.

Sound reaches the inner ear through the bone, so traffic, voices and alarms stay audible around you.

03 · LISTEN

A microphone on each side.

The one on your deaf side catches what you can't, and passes it across to your good ear.

04 · CHOOSE

Pick the voice. Feel the side.

A small chip lifts the voice you chose out of the noise. Gentle taps on the matching side show where a sound came from.

On you.

Soft silicone that sits behind your ear. Your ear stays open.

What goes where.

Four things in one band.

Everyday headphones

Connects over Bluetooth for music, calls and maps. Sound travels through your cheekbones.

Not part of this demo

Voice focus

Tap the person you want to hear. The room fades behind them.

Try it

Cross-ear hearing

A microphone on your deaf side catches sound and sends it to your good ear.

Try it

Direction buzz

A small tap on the side a sound came from, so you know where to look.

Before you start: headphones on.The demos send different sounds to each ear. Play each side below and check it comes from the right one.

A busy café, and one voice you want.

Four people are talking at once. Press play and try to follow Leo. Then switch Aura on and tap the person you want to hear.

Simulation: the voices are generated clips, and a real device would be less clean.

A sound on your deaf side.

Choose which ear can't hear. Then play a sound that happens on that side.

My deaf ear is
With Aura off, the demo plays nothing for the deaf side, to mimic what you would hear.

Where did that sound come from?

With one working ear, sounds seem to come from everywhere. Play a few and see if you can tell the side. Then switch Aura on.

Your headphones can’t vibrate from a web page. So with Aura on you get a low thump in the matching ear, a screen flash, and a real buzz on Android phones.
